introduction_markdown:
**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Physics 2 (0780), ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2024. Time allowed: three hours.**

Answer ALL questions. Section I is designed to be answered in 1 hour, Section II in 30 minutes and Section III in 1 hour. You are advised to divide your time accordingly. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. In calculations you must show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. Calculators and formulae booklet are allowed.

**Structure of the paper.** SECTION I (One hour): questions 1 to 5 are compulsory; in question 6 answer EITHER 6 (a), (b) and (c) OR 6 (d), (e) and (f). SECTION II (30 minutes): DATA ANALYSIS, question 7. SECTION III (1 hour): OPTIONS - answer any two questions from the four options (Option 1: Energy resources and environmental physics, question 8; Option 2: Communication, question 9; Option 3: Electronics, question 10; Option 4: Medical physics, question 11).

No data sheet is printed in the paper: whenever a constant is needed, the model answer states the value it uses.
enonce_intro_markdown:
Figure 1 shows a current-carrying solenoid wound on a steel rod.

![fig-1](gce-al-physics-2024-p2-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_1.png)

From Biot-Savart law, it can be shown that the size of the magnetic flux density ($B$) inside the solenoid is given by

$$B = \mu n I$$

Where $\mu$ is the permeability of the medium, $n$ is the number of turns of coil per unit length and $I$ is the current in the solenoid.

questions.enonce_markdown: Draw a diagram to show the magnetic flux pattern of the solenoid in figure 1.
questions.corrige_markdown:
The candidate draws the field lines; the expected pattern is as follows.

- **Inside the solenoid (and the steel rod):** straight, parallel, equally spaced lines along the axis, i.e. a **uniform** field. Because the steel has a very high relative permeability, the flux is concentrated in the rod and the lines are much closer together there than they would be in air.
- **Outside:** the lines leave the solenoid at one end (the north pole), spread out and curve round in smooth **closed loops** to re-enter at the other end (the south pole). The lines get further apart (the field gets weaker) away from the solenoid. The overall pattern is that of a bar magnet.
- Each line is a closed loop (inside the solenoid it runs from the south end to the north end) and two lines never cross.
- **Direction:** right-hand grip rule. Curl the fingers of the right hand round the turns in the direction of the conventional current; the thumb points along the axis to the **north** end, which is the direction of the lines inside the solenoid. Arrows are drawn on the lines pointing out of the north end and into the south end.

questions.enonce_markdown: Using only units, show that the above equation is homogeneous.
questions.corrige_markdown:
An equation is homogeneous when both sides have the same base units.

**Left-hand side.** From $F = BIL$,
$$[B] = \frac{\mathrm{N}}{\mathrm{A\,m}} = \frac{\mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-2}}}{\mathrm{A\,m}} = \mathrm{kg\,s^{-2}\,A^{-1}}\ \text{(tesla)}.$$

**Right-hand side.** The permeability has the unit of $\mu_0$. From the force per unit length between two long parallel wires, $\dfrac{F}{L} = \dfrac{\mu_0 I_1 I_2}{2\pi d}$, its unit is $\mathrm{N\,A^{-2}} = \mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-2}\,A^{-2}}$ (equivalent to $\mathrm{T\,m\,A^{-1}}$ or $\mathrm{H\,m^{-1}}$). The number of turns per unit length has the unit $\mathrm{m^{-1}}$ and the current $\mathrm{A}$. Hence
$$[\mu n I] = \mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-2}\,A^{-2}} \times \mathrm{m^{-1}} \times \mathrm{A} = \mathrm{kg\,s^{-2}\,A^{-1}}.$$

The two sides have the same base units, $\mathrm{kg\,s^{-2}\,A^{-1}}$, so the equation $B = \mu n I$ is homogeneous.

questions.enonce_markdown: If steel has a relative permeability of $2000$ and the above solenoid has $250$ turns, determine the magnetic field strength inside the solenoid.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Take $\mu_0 = 4\pi\times10^{-7}\ \mathrm{T\,m\,A^{-1}}$. From figure 1 the solenoid is $35.2\ \mathrm{cm} = 0.352\ \mathrm{m}$ long and carries $10.5\ \mathrm{A}$.

Turns per unit length:
$$n = \frac{N}{L} = \frac{250}{0.352} = 7.10\times10^{2}\ \mathrm{m^{-1}}.$$

Permeability of the steel:
$$\mu = \mu_r\mu_0 = 2000\times4\pi\times10^{-7} = 2.51\times10^{-3}\ \mathrm{T\,m\,A^{-1}}.$$

Magnetic flux density:
$$B = \mu n I = 2.51\times10^{-3}\times7.10\times10^{2}\times10.5 = 18.7\ \mathrm{T}.$$

**$B \approx 18.7\ \mathrm{T}$.** (If the "field strength" is taken as $H = nI$, then $H = 7.10\times10^{2}\times10.5 = 7.46\times10^{3}\ \mathrm{A\,m^{-1}}$, and $B = \mu H$ gives the same $18.7\ \mathrm{T}$. This value is far above the saturation flux density of real steel, about $2\ \mathrm{T}$; the question assumes a constant $\mu_r$.)
